summary: Doxylamine is a sedating first-generation ethanolamine H1 antihistamine. Over the counter, doxylamine succinate 25 mg is used as a short-term nighttime sleep aid to reduce difficulty falling asleep in adults and children 12 years and over. In combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) it is a recognized treatment for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. It has marked sedative and anticholinergic effects and should not be used in children under 12 for sleep.
indications: Short-term relief of difficulty falling asleep (nighttime sleep aid) in adults and children 12 years and over
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, in fixed combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6)

moa: Doxylamine is a competitive antagonist of histamine at peripheral and central H1 receptors. Its penetration of the blood-brain barrier and central H1 blockade produce sedation and reduce difficulty in falling asleep. It also has significant anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) activity, which contributes to its antiemetic effect and to side effects such as dry mouth and urinary retention.

preg: Doxylamine combined with pyridoxine is an established, recommended treatment for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy and has reassuring safety data. As an over-the-counter sleep aid, pregnant or breastfeeding women should ask a health professional before use.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding. Small amounts may pass into milk and can cause sedation or irritability in the infant, and antihistamines may reduce milk supply.
renal: Limited specific data; use with caution and at the lowest effective dose in renal impairment.
hepatic: Limited specific data; use with caution in hepatic impairment as metabolism may be reduced.

major: MAO inhibitors - prolong and intensify anticholinergic effects; avoid

missed: Doxylamine for sleep is taken only at bedtime when needed - if you forget and it is no longer near bedtime, skip it; do not take it during the day when you need to be alert. For the pregnancy combination, follow the product's missed-dose directions and do not double up.
overdose: Overdose causes anticholinergic toxicity: drowsiness or paradoxical excitation, dilated pupils, dry flushed skin, fever, tachycardia, urinary retention, hallucinations, and in severe cases seizures, coma and (particularly in massive overdose) rhabdomyolysis. Treatment is supportive: airway protection, activated charcoal if early, control of seizures and hyperthermia, and monitoring; there is no specific antidote.
